title: A prisoner swap but no breakthrough in Abu Dhabi, Ust-Luga on fire, and more ships hit in the Gulf
summary: The Abu Dhabi talks end with a prisoner exchange deal and no movement on a ceasefire, Ukrainian drones set Russia's Ust-Luga oil port ablaze while a Russian drone kills three at a market near Odesa, tankers are hit around the Strait of Hormuz and an ADNOC vessel is attacked in UAE waters, Iran denies it is talking to Washington, and Riyadh intercepts Houthi missiles for a second day.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Welcome to the ForceFinder Daily Briefing. I'm Avery.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And I'm Cole. As always, this show is generated automatically from the open-source reporting behind the ForceFinder map. Every story has source links on the globe, so treat us as a guide, not the final word.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: It's Wednesday, November eleventh. The Abu Dhabi talks between Russia and Ukraine have wrapped up. And there is one concrete result.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: A prisoner exchange. Both sides agreed to what's being described as a large swap of prisoners of war. Russia's chief negotiator, Vladimir Medinsky, said the numbers and the procedure will come later.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: But that was the only concrete result. Euronews reports there was no breakthrough on a ceasefire, or on territory. And the second day was short. Russian state media said it lasted about two hours.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: The next step is in Moscow. The American envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, plan to meet President Putin on Thursday.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And on the question we've been following all week, who's in the room. European officials were in Abu Dhabi, but they held separate consultations. They did not join the three-way talks.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: There's an interesting read on that from the Institute for the Study of War. It assesses that the Kremlin is trying to turn these talks into a negotiation about European security more broadly, reviving demands it made about NATO back in twenty twenty-one.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And on the battlefield, the Institute says neither side advanced on Tuesday. So the front line is static, while the air war is anything but.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Right. Overnight, Ukrainian drones hit Ust-Luga, Russia's largest port on the Baltic and a major oil export hub.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: The regional governor, Aleksandr Drozdenko, says the strike started a fire, knocked out a substation and injured three workers. He says a hundred and fifty drones were shot down over the Leningrad region.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: That's the same region where the Kirishi refinery was set on fire two days ago. And the Baltic states issued drone alerts overnight.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Further south, in Russia's Smolensk region, the governor says two people were killed when debris from a Ukrainian drone hit an apartment building in the town of Yartsevo and started a fire.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: In Ukraine, the worst single incident was in Chornomorsk, the port town near Odesa. Regional officials say a Russian jet-powered drone hit a market, killing three people and wounding eleven.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Ukraine says Russia launched a hundred and sixty-three drones and cruise missiles overnight. Two of those missiles crossed into Moldova's airspace. And across the country, regional authorities counted nine people killed and thirty-nine injured over the day.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: So, a prisoner deal on paper, and both sides striking each other's ports the same night.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Let's move to the Gulf, where shipping took more hits. On Tuesday, the British maritime agency UKMTO said a tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile about nineteen nautical miles northeast of Limah, in Oman. The crew was reported safe.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: The same afternoon, the Emirati company ADNOC Logistics and Services said one of its vessels was damaged in an attack inside the United Arab Emirates' own waters. It didn't name the ship or say who was responsible. The Emirati government called it a grave threat to navigation.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And today, Iran's navy said an oil tanker caught fire after hitting a mine in what it called a restricted area east of the strait. UKMTO issued a warning about a tanker incident, but didn't confirm the cause.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: A maritime security firm, Vanguard Tech, identified one vessel as the Saudi-flagged NCC Fajr and described a possible attack. As usual with these, the mine claims come from Iran and haven't been independently verified.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: On the diplomacy, there's a real gap between what Washington and Tehran are saying. Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, called American claims of ongoing talks, or of a planned meeting in Qatar, complete lies.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: At the same time, Iran's foreign minister says its two-day proposal still stands. And Qatar, the go-between, says it's had positive responses from both sides.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So the channel through Qatar seems to be alive, even if Iran won't call it talks.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Now Saudi Arabia and the Houthis. Today the Saudi-led coalition said its air defences intercepted three Houthi cruise missiles aimed at the Riyadh region. No casualties or damage were reported.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: That's the second day running. On Tuesday, Saudi air defences intercepted a ballistic missile and a cruise missile heading for Riyadh.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: The Houthis say they carried out four operations on Tuesday, against Aramco facilities, Riyadh's main airport, pumping stations on the East-West oil pipeline, and Saudi forces inside Yemen. Saudi Arabia hasn't confirmed those.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: In Gaza, local health officials say Israeli airstrikes killed three Palestinians today, including two brothers. One strike hit a rooftop in Gaza City, and another hit a tent for displaced people in Sheikh Radwan. The Israeli military didn't comment.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And in Sudan, Sudan Tribune reports that a drone attack by the Rapid Support Forces killed nine civilians in a village in the Blue Nile region on Tuesday.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: On the ships, no confirmed changes today. The Theodore Roosevelt was last reported leaving Singapore and heading west toward the Middle East, so its position on the map is still an estimate. Two carriers, the George Washington and the George H. W. Bush, remain in the Arabian Sea.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: One note for regular users of the site. There's a new Strike data section in the sidebar. It keeps a permanent record of the strikes on the map, lets you chart them, for example by nearest city or by who fired, and you can download the whole thing as a spreadsheet file.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So, what to watch. Thursday's meeting between the American envoys and Putin in Moscow, and the details of that prisoner exchange. Whether the attacks on shipping in the Gulf keep widening. And whether Iran's two-day proposal goes anywhere.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: That's the briefing. Thanks for listening, and we'll see you tomorrow.
